note: The triage question set. Each question is bounded (fixed answer set) and gets only the state fields it needs (state_fields); applies_when names predicates in runner/common.py (all must hold). Bump a question's 'version' when you change its wording, options or state: results are keyed by (line id, question id, version), so a changed question is re-asked and old answers are kept but ignored. 'problem' says which answer means 'something is wrong' (used by the report and the calibration).

questions.question: Does the English line convey the same meaning as the Japanese line: the same facts, the same speech act (question, refusal, tease, apology...) and the same intent, allowing natural rewording, reordering, and dropped filler particles?
questions.guidance: Name tokens in brackets are filled in by the game at run time and are not errors. A reply menu (Reply 1 / Reply 2 ...) is judged reply by reply.

questions.question: Given the speaker's voice note, how does the English line's register fit that character?

option_descriptions.matches_voice: sounds like this character as the voice note describes
option_descriptions.too_formal: stiffer or more polite than this character would be here
option_descriptions.too_casual: looser, slangier or ruder than this character would be here
option_descriptions.wrong_character_voice: sounds like a different character (e.g. another heroine's signature words or tics)

questions.question: For every Japanese glossary term listed, does the English line use the glossary's English rendering (or a natural inflection or short form the glossary note allows)?
How natural is the English as something this kind of speaker would actually say or a game would display?

scale_labels.0: broken: ungrammatical or hard to understand

questions.question: Does the English text contain untranslated Japanese, romanized Japanese where plain English was expected, placeholder or note text, a broken control code, or garbled characters?
questions.guidance: Allowed on purpose: Senpai (Yumi Saotome only), Sensei, giri-choco, bunkasai, omikuji, prf, and the {tokens} the game fills in.

questions.question: Does the English line follow the style guide's policy on honorifics and forms of address?

option_descriptions.follows_policy: the line follows the policy (or has nothing the policy governs)
option_descriptions.honorific_kept: a -san / -kun / -chan / -sama suffix the policy drops is in the English
option_descriptions.senpai_misused: 'Senpai' is used by someone other than Yumi Saotome, or Yumi's 先輩 form of address was lost
option_descriptions.address_handwritten: the player's name or a form of address is typed into the line instead of the game's token, or a name token was dropped
option_descriptions.teacher_title_wrong: 先生 is not rendered as Mr./Ms. Surname (or Sensei for a coach)

questions.question: Compared with the Japanese, has the English changed the mood or intent of the line: an insult softened or sharpened, a joke added, sincerity turned ironic or campy, a tease turned into an attack, or the emotional beat order changed?
Do the English replies keep the contrast between the Japanese replies (for example sincere vs cocky vs dismissive), so the player can predict how the girl will react to each?
Should a human editor look at this line before release (any doubt about meaning, voice, tone, terminology, or how it reads in context)?
